recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit as-is. It completes the narrow metadata correction directly attributable to FHIR-38991; any future migration from RFC 7231 references to newer HTTP RFCs should be handled across the full page under a separate tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-38991 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested adding Location and Content-Location to the RESTful API HTTP Headers table, linking that table to Custom Headers, adding matching metadata columns to the Custom Headers table, and adding X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Port, and X-Forwarded-Prefix.
initial_application: Git commit d1399f74f158a7e810db07f8f79052c9b3ecd721 initially applied FHIR-38991 by adding the requested rows, cross-link, and Custom Headers columns. The current source showed that this application left incomplete or inconsistent table metadata: missing MDN links for Location and Content-Location, a malformed displayed RFC section for Location, and 'both' directions for the new X-Forwarded routing headers.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active RESTful API page source because publish.ini maps http.html to the http page. FHIR-I minutes for 2022-10-24 confirm the Persuasive with Modification vote and summarize the issue as adding Location and Content-Location. Jira and community searches found no later issue or discussion that changed the requested HTTP header table semantics.
reconciliation: Edited source/http.html so Location and Content-Location have MDN links, Location's RFC label reads RFC-7231 section 7.1.2, and X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Port, and X-Forwarded-Prefix are marked as request headers consistent with the adjacent X-Forwarded rows and their routing metadata descriptions.
source_changes: source/http.html: added MDN links for the Location and Content-Location response header rows.
source/http.html: corrected the Location RFC display label from RFC-7231 section 37.1.2 to section 7.1.2.
source/http.html: changed X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Port, and X-Forwarded-Prefix directions from both to request.
